rubric: PYTHON AS A FIRST LANGUAGE / EXCEPTIONS AND FILES / CHAPTER 15

slides.title: Exceptions
slides.main: A real program anticipates failures and copes, rather than falling apart.

items.title: Catching
items.sub: Catch the error and go on

slides.title: Reading a traceback
slides.sub: Bottom up: error type, then call chain
slides.main: The error type is a hint: IndexError, KeyError, TypeError, ValueError, ZeroDivisionError.

body.text:
nums = [1, 2, 3]
print(nums[5])
ON SCREEN

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "main.py", line 2, in <module>
    print(nums[5])
IndexError: list index out of range

slides.title: try and except
slides.sub: Risky code in try, reaction in except
slides.main: Catch a specific error type: unexpected ones should still fail loudly.

body.text: ON SCREEN

that is not a number
the program is alive
Keep the try block short: only lines that can really fail.

slides.title: Several excepts and as
slides.sub: Top to bottom: the first match runs
slides.main: A bare except hides real errors; for almost everything, catch Exception.

slides.title: else and finally
slides.sub: else if no error, finally always
slides.main: finally is for cleanup: close a file, free a resource, log the result.

slides.title: Raising exceptions: raise
slides.sub: As early and as precisely as possible
slides.main: A bare raise in except passes the error on with its whole traceback.

slides.title: Custom exceptions
slides.main: One base class for a library's errors: catch one case or the whole family.

slides.title: Exception hierarchy
slides.main: Specific excepts first, general after; KeyboardInterrupt is apart from Exception.

body.text:
print(issubclass(KeyError, LookupError), issubclass(IndexError, LookupError))
print(issubclass(ZeroDivisionError, ArithmeticError))
print(issubclass(KeyboardInterrupt, Exception))

try:
    {}["x"]
except LookupError:
    print("caught via the ancestor")

slides.title: EAFP: ask forgiveness, not permission
slides.sub: Check first, or try and catch
slides.main: For files, open and catch: while you checked, the file could be deleted.

body.text:
d = {"a": 1}
if "b" in d:           # check first
    print(d["b"])

try:                   # or just try
    print(d["b"])
except KeyError:
    print("no such key")
ON SCREEN
no such key
Rare, alarming error: exception; frequent, normal: get or a check.

slides.title: Chaining: raise from
slides.sub: Make a clear error without losing the cause
slides.main: A handler must not silently swallow: fix it, raise it on, or rename it.

body.text: ON SCREEN
no port in the settings | cause: KeyError('port')

slides.title: assert and raise
slides.main: assert is off under optimization: never validate user data with it.

slides.title: Common mistakes
slides.main: Catch only what you can handle; let the rest crash loudly.

body.text:
try:
    risky()
except:          # a bare except catches everything
    pass         # and stays silent: the worst option

print("all fine?")
ON SCREEN
all fine?
Also: a huge try, raise e instead of raise, return in finally, assert instead of input checks.

slides.title: Summary
slides.main: Catch only what you can handle.
